quote: If we had no winter the spring would not be so pleasant: if we did not sometimes tast of adversity, prosperity would not be so welcome.
source: Anne Bradstreet, Meditations Divine and Moral, meditation XIV (ed. J. H. Ellis, 1867), p. 51

evidence.where: two archive.org OCR copies of Ellis's 1867 Works of Anne Bradstreet in Prose and Verse (cu31924021996354 and worksofannebrads00brad), meditations read in sequence
evidence.edition: The Works of Anne Bradstreet in Prose and Verse, ed. John Harvard Ellis, Charlestown, Abram E. Cutter, 1867
evidence.locator: Meditations Diuine and morall, XIV, p. 51 (running head Meditations. 51 above it)

reason: Ellis prints XIV as proposed, colon and the spelling tast included (the OCR reads the long s as f or l); only the long s is modernised. The source uses the house form from May's Bradstreet line. Not shipped, nothing near, Bradstreet at 2 of 3, not banned.
